distinct_activities: ADP-ribosyl cyclase (NAD+ -> cyclic ADP-ribose + nicotinamide, EC 3.2.2.6)
cyclic ADP-ribose hydrolase (cADPR + H2O -> ADP-ribose), the reaction scored here
organism_context: mammals: CD38 and the paralogue BST-1/CD157; the Aplysia homologue is cyclase-dominant with little hydrolase activity
rationale: The equation is cADPR + H2O -> ADP-ribose, the cADPR hydrolase half-reaction of CD38, an ectoenzyme that both synthesises cADPR from NAD+ and hydrolyses it to ADP-ribose; the two activities are regulated independently in the same protein. Enzyme assignment is inferred from the chemistry (MetaCyc RXN-13873 carries no EC in the snapshot), hence medium confidence.
direction_note: CD38 both makes and destroys cADPR, but it does so by two different reactions; the hydrolysis written here is an irreversible glycosidic hydrolysis, so the forward (LLM) direction is the only one the enzyme supports.

organism_context: Daphne spp. (MetaCyc PWY-7056, daphnin interconversion)
rationale: The chemistry is hydrolysis of the 7-O-glucoside daphnin to D-glucose + daphnetin, i.e. a beta-glucosidase, but no specific protein, gene or structural paper could be found in PubMed/Europe PMC for the Daphne daphnin glucosidase, so functionality is left unknown rather than assumed.
direction_note: ModelSEED's reverse call would require condensing free D-glucose with daphnetin; no enzyme does that (glucosylation runs from UDP-glucose), so only the hydrolytic (forward) direction is enzymologically real.

enzyme_name: ovothiol A Npi-methyltransferase (C-terminal methyltransferase domain of OvoA)
distinct_activities: 5-histidylcysteine sulfoxide synthase (mononuclear non-heme iron oxidase domain)
SAM-dependent thioimidazole Npi-methyltransferase (the reaction scored here)
organism_context: most ovothiol producers (bacteria, marine invertebrates, Trypanosoma) carry OvoA as a single dual-domain chain; a separate clade (OvoM) and the Hydrogenimonas thermophila enzyme OvoATh2 have the two activities on separate proteins
rationale: Ireland et al. show that ovothiol Npi-methyltransferases are normally fused as a C-terminal domain to the sulfoxide synthase OvoA, with standalone OvoMs being the exception; so the enzyme methylating 5-thiohistidine (mercaptohistidine) to ovothiol is usually one domain of a genuinely bifunctional polypeptide.
direction_note: The methyltransferase domain runs an irreversible SAM -> SAH methyl transfer; ModelSEED's reverse call would be an SAH-driven demethylation, which this enzyme cannot do.

enzyme_name: none identified - spontaneous lactonisation of (Z)-2,4-dihydroxycinnamate to umbelliferone
organism_context: plant coumarin biosynthesis (MetaCyc COUMARIN-SYN / PWY-7186)
rationale: Ring closure of the cis-2'-hydroxy-cinnamate to the coumarin lactone is generally treated as a non-enzymatic step downstream of the 2'-hydroxylase/isomerase in coumarin biosynthesis; no catalysing protein could be identified, so functionality is unknown.
direction_note: The snapshot status is MI:H:-1/O:-1|CI:1 - the water released on lactonisation is missing from the equation, which is what makes the computed dG look like it favours ring opening; the coumarin lactone is the thermodynamically stable form.

enzyme_name: cephalosporin-C deacetylase (acetyl esterase, carbohydrate esterase family 7)
organism_context: Bacillus subtilis and other Bacillaceae; CE7 members are routinely annotated both as cephalosporin-C deacetylase and acetyl xylan esterase
rationale: A single acetyl esterase active site hydrolyses the 3'-acetyl ester of cephalosporin C; the parallel 'acetyl xylan esterase' name reflects substrate promiscuity of that one esterase activity, not a second catalytic function, so this stays monofunctional.
direction_note: The deacetylated product (deacetylcephalosporin C) is absent from the equation (status MI:C:-14/H:-17/N:-3/O:-7/S:-1), so the half-equation ModelSEED scored is not a usable basis for a direction; an esterase only hydrolyses.

organism_context: Psilocybe cubensis and other psilocybin-producing agarics
rationale: PsiK is a small ATP-dependent 4-O-kinase of the aminoglycoside-phosphotransferase fold with a single kinase active site; structural work on substrate recognition reports no second catalytic activity, and it phosphorylates psilocin back to psilocybin.
direction_note: ATP-driven phosphotransfer to a phenol is effectively irreversible; the reverse (ADP phosphorylation by psilocybin) is not a PsiK activity - dephosphorylation of psilocybin is done by a separate phosphatase.

distinct_activities: aspartate carbamoyltransferase (EC 2.1.3.2), the reaction scored here
organism_context: metazoa: the three activities are fused in CAD (and in yeast URA2 as a CPSase-ATCase fusion); in E. coli the ATCase catalytic chain PyrB is a separate polypeptide that assembles with the regulatory chain PyrI - a multi-subunit holoenzyme, not a fusion
rationale: The reaction is the classic ATCase step; in animals it is one domain of the trifunctional CAD polypeptide, while in bacteria it is the standalone PyrB catalytic subunit of a c6r6 holoenzyme (a complex, which per protocol is not counted as bifunctional). Lineage-restricted fusion is scored as polyfunctional.
direction_note: N-carbamoyl-L-aspartate is missing from the equation (status MI:C:-5/H:-7/N:-2/O:-5), which is why the computed dG is strongly positive; the real ATCase step is the committed, effectively irreversible entry into pyrimidine biosynthesis and runs forward.

organism_context: Fusarium heterosporum equisetin (eqx) cluster; the homologous Fusarium fujikuroi cluster lacks eqxD and therefore stops at the N-desmethyl product trichosetin
rationale: Janevska et al. identify eqxD as the equisetin N-methyltransferase gene and show that the F. fujikuroi cluster, which lacks it, accumulates trichosetin (= N-desmethylequisetin); EqxD is a discrete small cluster gene separate from the PKS-NRPS, with no second activity reported.
direction_note: SAM-dependent N-methylation of a tetramic acid is irreversible; the reverse direction ModelSEED recommends has no enzymatic counterpart.

enzyme_name: no single enzyme - the GDP-D-alpha-D-octose to methylthiolincosamide segment of lincomycin A biosynthesis
organism_context: Streptomyces lincolnensis (MetaCyc PWY-7548)
rationale: GDP-D-alpha-D-octose was identified by Lin et al. as an intermediate several steps upstream of methylthiolincosamide; converting it to MTL requires nucleotide release and thiol transfer via ergothioneine/mycothiol carriers, transamination and S-methylation by distinct Lmb proteins, so no one enzyme catalyses the entry as written.
direction_note: The entry collapses a multi-enzyme biosynthetic segment (status MI:C:-9/H:-6/N:-4/O:-13/P:-2/S:1); the pathway flux runs GDP-octose -> MTL, i.e. the direction the council picked, but no single-enzyme direction can be assigned.

distinct_activities: adenylyl-sulfate kinase (EC 2.7.1.25), the reaction scored here
organism_context: animals and many fungi/protists carry the fused PAPS synthase (human PAPSS1/PAPSS2; also the bacterial CysNC fusion); E. coli CysC and yeast Met14 are standalone APS kinases
rationale: In PAPS synthases the APS kinase and ATP sulfurylase activities sit on one polypeptide (N-terminal APS kinase domain, C-terminal sulfurylase domain), a genuine fusion rather than a complex; in bacteria and yeast the same kinase activity is a standalone protein.
direction_note: PAPS is missing from the equation (status MI:C:-10/H:-12/N:-5/O:-13/P:-2/S:-1); physiologically the APS kinase domain pulls the unfavourable sulfurylase step forward by consuming APS, so flux runs APS -> PAPS, the LLM direction.

organism_context: Streptomyces hygroscopicus; the hph resistance gene is the common eukaryotic selection marker
rationale: A single aminoglycoside-phosphotransferase-fold kinase domain; unlike the well-known AAC(6')-Ie/APH(2'')-Ia fusion among aminoglycoside-modifying enzymes, hygromycin B kinase carries only the kinase activity.
direction_note: Phosphohygromycin B is missing from the equation (status MI:C:-20/H:-39/N:-3/O:-16/P:-1); an ATP-dependent antibiotic-inactivating kinase only phosphorylates, so the forward direction is the only enzymatic one.

organism_context: human NUDT5; related oxidised-nucleotide sanitising Nudix enzymes (MTH1/NUDT1, MutT) in other organisms
rationale: Arimori et al. show human NUDT5 hydrolyses 8-oxo-dADP (as well as 8-oxo-dGDP and ADP-ribose) in one Nudix active site; broad substrate recognition within one hydrolase activity is not bifunctionality, and the reported nuclear ATP-forming activity is the same chemistry run backwards, not a second activity.
direction_note: The two ModelSEED compounds do not correspond (cpd25973 8-OH-dADP is C10H11N4O11P2 vs cpd34577 8-oxo-dAMP C10H12N5O7P; status MI:H:1/N:1/O:-1), so the scored dG is for a nonsense transformation; the real enzyme is a one-way sanitising hydrolase.

organism_context: Kribbella flavida NBRC 14399T; the downstream isomaltose glucohydrolase Kfla1896 (GH15) is a separate protein
rationale: Tagami et al. show Kfla1895 hydrolyses the alpha-(1->3) linkage of the cyclic tetrasaccharide CNN, opening it to the linear tetrasaccharide written here before further degradation; it is a single-active-site glycoside hydrolase.
direction_note: Ring opening of a cyclic glucotetraose by a glycoside hydrolase is the catabolic direction; the reverse (re-cyclisation of a free tetrasaccharide with loss of water) is done by transferases from starch, not by this hydrolase.

organism_context: yeast GNA1, human GNPNAT1, and bacterial/fungal homologues; a homodimeric GNAT-fold acetyltransferase
rationale: A single GNAT acetyl-CoA-dependent acetyltransferase active site converts glucosamine-6-phosphate to N-acetylglucosamine-6-phosphate; no second catalytic activity is reported for GNA1-family proteins.
direction_note: N-acetyl-D-glucosamine phosphate is missing from the equation (status MI:C:-8/H:-14/N:-1/O:-9/P:-1); thioester-to-amide acyl transfer is strongly exergonic and physiologically one-way, so the forward direction is correct.

organism_context: bacterial Dps 12-mers (E. coli, Deinococcus, Marinobacter); classical 24-mer ferritins run the same ferroxidation with O2 rather than H2O2
rationale: Dps ferroxidase centres oxidise two Fe(II) per H2O2 and deposit the FeO(OH) mineral core inside the cage; its DNA-binding/protection role is structural, not catalytic, and so is excluded as moonlighting, leaving one catalytic activity.
direction_note: Fe(II) oxidation by H2O2 is strongly exergonic and the mineral core does not redissolve through the ferroxidase site, so the reverse direction ModelSEED recommends is not an enzymatic reaction; the dGPredictor value (+118 kJ/mol) is an artefact of group-contribution on a mineral pseudo-compound.

enzyme_name: no single enzyme - the 3-(4-sulfophenyl)butanoate to 4-sulfoacetophenone segment of LAS surfactant degradation
organism_context: Comamonas testosteroni KF-1 (MetaCyc PWY-7521)
rationale: Schleheck et al. identified 4-sulfoacetophenone as a transient intermediate several enzymatic steps downstream of 3-(4-sulfophenyl)butyrate (loss of a C2 unit before the Baeyer-Villiger monooxygenase/esterase pair acts), so the entry lumps a multi-enzyme catabolic segment rather than one reaction.
direction_note: Status MI:C:-2/H:-3/O:-1 confirms a C2 fragment is unaccounted for; catabolic flux runs toward 4-sulfoacetophenone, so the council's forward call matches the pathway even though no single enzyme catalyses the lumped step.

organism_context: Brassicaceae; sinalbin (p-hydroxybenzylglucosinolate) is the Sinapis alba product, the Arabidopsis orthologues SOT16/17/18 were characterised kinetically
rationale: Cytosolic PAPS-dependent sulfotransferases of the SOT16-18 family carry a single sulfuryl-transfer active site; Klein and Papenbrock characterised all three as sulfotransferases differing only in substrate preference.
direction_note: PAPS -> PAP sulfuryl transfer is strongly exergonic and physiologically irreversible; the reverse would require PAP-driven desulfation, which these enzymes do not catalyse.

enzyme_name: manganese oxidase (multicopper oxidase MnxG / CotA / MofA / MoxA)
organism_context: Mn(II)-oxidising bacteria; in Bacillus sp. PL-12 MnxG acts within the MnxE/MnxF/MnxG complex, while Bacillus subtilis CotA is a single-chain spore-coat laccase
rationale: KEGG EC 1.16.3.3 is manganese oxidase, a multicopper oxidase that oxidises Mn(II) to insoluble Mn(IV) oxide; the two sequential one-electron oxidations occur at one multicopper site, and the Mnx arrangement is a multi-subunit complex rather than a fused bifunctional chain.
direction_note: The equation matches the IUBMB/KEGG reaction exactly and is balanced; biological Mn oxidation runs only toward the MnO2 mineral, so ModelSEED's reverse call (reductive dissolution of MnO2 releasing O2) has no enzymatic basis.

enzyme_name: methylarsonate (MMA(V)) reductase = omega-class glutathione transferase GSTO1-1
distinct_activities: monomethylarsonate reductase (EC 1.20.4.2), the reaction scored here
organism_context: human GSTO1-1 (hGSTO1); allelic variants differ in both reductase activities
rationale: Zakharyan et al. identified human MMA(V) reductase as an omega-class GST, and Schmuck et al. assayed its monomethylarsonate reductase and dehydroascorbate reductase activities side by side; these are distinct catalytic activities on one 241-residue chain, though they share the single Cys32 active site rather than sitting on separate fused domains.
direction_note: Glutathione disulfide and water are missing from the equation (status MI:C:-20/H:-27/N:-6/O:-13/S:-2), so the +216 kJ/mol dG is meaningless; the detoxification flux is MMA(V) -> MMA(III), the forward direction.

organism_context: benzylisoquinoline alkaloid metabolism; the characterised plant coclaurine N-methyltransferases act on (S)-substrates, so the protein assigned to the (R)-enantiomer could not be pinned down
rationale: The chemistry is a SAM-dependent secondary-amine N-methylation of a 1-benzyltetrahydroisoquinoline, i.e. a CNMT-family methyltransferase, but no publication could be found assigning a specific protein to the (R)-norlaudanosoline substrate of MetaCyc RXN-19910, so functionality is left unknown.
direction_note: Whatever the protein, SAM-dependent N-methylation is irreversible in the SAM -> SAH direction, so ModelSEED's reverse call cannot be right.

organism_context: cofactor-free homotetrameric uricases of bacteria, fungi, plants and most mammals; the downstream HIU hydrolase and OHCU decarboxylase are separate proteins
rationale: Urate oxidase is a cofactor-free oxidase with one active site producing 5-hydroxyisourate and H2O2; the subsequent hydrolysis/decarboxylation to allantoin is carried out by distinct enzymes (or spontaneously), so there is no second activity on this chain.
direction_note: 5-hydroxyisourate is missing from the equation (status MI:C:-5/H:-3/N:-4/O:-4), which inflates the apparent dG; O2-dependent oxidation of urate is irreversible, so the forward direction is correct.

organism_context: Chondromyces crocatus Cm c5 chondrochloren (cnd) biosynthetic cluster
rationale: The chondrochloren cluster has been studied mainly for its halogenase CndH and the oxidative decarboxylase CndG; the methyltransferase converting chondrochloren A to B has not been characterised, which is consistent with MetaCyc's placeholder EC 2.1.1.M7, so the enzyme and its functionality are unknown.
direction_note: SAM-dependent methylation runs one way (SAM -> SAH); the reverse call would require SAH-dependent demethylation, which no methyltransferase performs.

organism_context: Aspergillus fumigatus gli cluster; the unrelated bis-thiomethyltransferase GtmA is a separate protein acting on the thiols
rationale: Scharf et al. showed GliN is the SAM-dependent amide N-methyltransferase that converts N-desmethylgliotoxin to gliotoxin (and that the S-methylation by GtmA has the opposite, inactivating effect); GliN is a standalone single-activity methyltransferase.
direction_note: N-methylation by GliN is an irreversible biosynthetic maturation step required for gliotoxin's activity, so the forward direction is the only one supported.

organism_context: sulfate-reducing enrichment culture N47 (Deltaproteobacteria); a ~750 kDa multi-subunit complex, not a fused multidomain chain
rationale: Mouttaki et al. demonstrated the carboxylation biochemically in N47 cell extracts and Koelschbach et al. identified the subunits of the ~750 kDa UbiD-like complex; the activities are distributed over separate polypeptides, so per protocol the catalysing subunit is scored monofunctional.
direction_note: The enzyme exchanges 13C-bicarbonate into the carboxyl group of 2-naphthoate 27x faster than it carboxylates naphthalene net, and dG'o is only about +3 kJ/mol, so the carboxylation/decarboxylation step is freely reversible at the active site and the net direction is set by bicarbonate levels and downstream pull, not by the enzyme.

organism_context: Fusarium fujikuroi / Fusarium spp. fsr naphthoquinone cluster (MetaCyc PWY-7689)
rationale: Studt et al. assigned the fsr cluster genes to fusarubin biosynthesis but several late interconversions in their proposed scheme are not matched to a specific protein; the interconversion of 8-O-methyl-13-carboxynorjavanicin and 8-O-methylfusarubinlactone has no identified catalyst and may be a spontaneous ring-chain tautomerisation.
direction_note: The two species are formula isomers differing only by the proton (no water exchanged), i.e. a pH-dependent lactone/open-acid equilibrium; with no enzyme identified there is no enzymology to favour either side, although MetaCyc writes the biosynthetic flow toward the lactone.
